```{python}
import json
from html import escape
from pathlib import Path

import plotly.express as px
import polars as pl
from great_tables import GT
from IPython.display import display

comparison = json.loads(Path("comparison.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
runs = comparison["runs"]


def show_table(frame):
    table = GT(frame)
    strings = [name for name, dtype in frame.schema.items() if dtype == pl.String]
    numbers = [name for name, dtype in frame.schema.items() if dtype.is_float()]
    if strings:
        table = table.fmt(escape, columns=strings)
    if numbers:
        table = table.fmt_number(columns=numbers, decimals=4)
    costs = [name for name in ("USD total", "Known USD", "Known USD per 1,000") if name in frame.columns]
    if costs:
        table = table.fmt_number(columns=costs, decimals=6)
    if "Additional request USD" in frame.columns:
        table = table.fmt_number(columns="Additional request USD", decimals=9)
    display(table)


show_table(pl.DataFrame({"Comparison": [comparison["title"]]}))
show_table(pl.DataFrame([
    {"Run": run["label"], "Experiment": run.get("title", run["path"])}
    for run in runs
]))
```

This report reads saved predictions and makes no provider calls. It compares the
same selected source records across runs. It does not select prompts or routing
thresholds, or establish statistical significance. Mock runs test the pipeline.

## Data compatibility

```{python}
print(f"Selected records per run: {runs[0]['metrics']['support']}")
print(f"Selected dataset SHA256: {comparison['dataset_sha256']}")
if comparison["historical_inputs_verified"]:
    print("Historical inputs verified: current selected data match every run's saved fingerprint.")
else:
    print("Historical inputs unverified for legacy runs:")
    for warning in comparison["warnings"]:
        print(warning)
if runs[0]["metrics"]["support"] < 30:
    print("Small smoke sample: use these results to check the pipeline, not to rank model quality.")
```

## Overall comparison

Accuracy and macro F1 include unresolved predictions in their denominators.
Coverage is the fraction with a resolved prediction. Latency reflects recorded
provider requests, including the original timing when predictions came from cache;
it is not the elapsed time of generating this report.

```{python}
summary = pl.DataFrame([
    {
        "Run": run["label"], "Display": f"{run['label']}: {run['provider']}",
        "Provider": run["provider"], "Model": run["model"],
        "Simulated": run["simulated"], "Records": run["metrics"]["support"],
        "Accuracy": run["metrics"]["accuracy"],
        "Macro F1": run["metrics"]["macro_f1"],
        "Coverage": run["metrics"]["operational_coverage"],
        "P50 ms": run["metrics"]["latency_p50_ms"],
        "P95 ms": run["metrics"]["latency_p95_ms"],
        "USD total": run["metrics"]["cost_usd_total"],
        "Known USD": run["metrics"]["cost_usd_known_total"],
        "Known USD per 1,000": (
            run["metrics"]["cost_usd_known_total"] * 1000 / run["metrics"]["support"]
        ),
        "Cost status": (
            "Complete" if run["metrics"]["cost_priced_fraction"] == 1
            else "Partial (lower bound)" if run["metrics"]["cost_priced_fraction"] > 0
            else "No pricing available"
        ),
        "USD per 1,000": run["metrics"]["cost_usd_per_1000"],
        "Priced fraction": run["metrics"]["cost_priced_fraction"],
    }
    for run in runs
], schema_overrides={"USD total": pl.Float64, "USD per 1,000": pl.Float64})
show_table(summary.select("Run", "Provider", "Model", "Records", "Accuracy", "Macro F1", "Coverage"))
```

## Latency

```{python}
show_table(summary.select("Run", "P50 ms", "P95 ms"))
show_table(pl.DataFrame([
    {"Run": run["label"], "Latency scope": run.get("latency_scope", "Not recorded")}
    for run in runs
]))
```

## Cost accounting

Known cost includes every cost estimate present in the saved predictions, including
failed attempts when their costs were retained. A complete total requires every
record to be priced. Missing costs are unknown, not free; a partial known cost is
only a lower bound. Failed-call usage recovered in a separate audit is not silently
added to the original benchmark. Recollection costs are included when recorded in
the derived predictions, as described in each run's accounting scope below.

```{python}
show_table(summary.select("Run", "Cost status", "Known USD", "USD total", "Priced fraction"))
show_table(pl.DataFrame([
    {
        "Run": run["label"],
        "Cost and usage scope": run.get("cost_and_usage_scope", "Not recorded"),
        "Collection policy": run.get("collection_policy", "Not recorded"),
    }
    for run in runs
]))
```

```{python}
recollections = [
    {
        "Run": run["label"], "Fresh attempts": run.get("recollection_attempts"),
        "Additional request USD": run.get("recollection_cost_usd"),
    }
    for run in runs if run.get("recollection_attempts") is not None
]
if recollections:
    show_table(pl.DataFrame(recollections, schema_overrides={"Additional request USD": pl.Float64}))
```

Additional request USD comes from the saved recollection audit. It is already
included in the derived run's cost, not an amount to add again. A missing value
means no complete recollection-cost total was recorded. The difference between
run totals need not equal new spend when the original run had missing costs.

These are token-based USD estimates for the saved results, not billing statements
or new spend from generating the comparison. Runs can share cached calls and
ancestry: **do not add their totals together to calculate new spend**.

```{python}
priced = summary.filter(pl.col("Priced fraction") > 0)
if priced.height:
    fig = px.bar(
        priced, x="Display", y="Known USD per 1,000", color="Cost status",
        labels={"Display": "Run"},
        pattern_shape="Cost status",
        hover_data=["Provider", "Model", "Known USD", "Priced fraction"],
        title="Recorded cost per 1,000 records; partial bars are lower bounds",
    )
    fig.show(renderer="notebook")
for row in summary.filter(pl.col("Priced fraction") == 0).iter_rows(named=True):
    print(f"{row['Run']}: No pricing available; no zero-cost bar is shown.")
```

## Quality versus cost and latency

A partial-cost point may move to the right if missing costs are recovered. Do not
rank it as cheaper than another run using the lower bound alone. The latency plot
uses recorded timings; recollected runs can lack original rejected-attempt times,
so compare their latency scopes before interpreting small differences.

```{python}
if priced.height:
    fig = px.scatter(
        priced, x="Known USD per 1,000", y="Macro F1", color="Display",
        labels={"Display": "Run"},
        symbol="Cost status",
        hover_data=["Provider", "Model", "Accuracy", "Coverage", "Records", "Priced fraction"],
        symbol_map={"Complete": "circle", "Partial (lower bound)": "triangle-right"},
        title="Macro F1 versus recorded cost; partial points are lower bounds",
    )
    fig.update_traces(marker_size=14)
    fig.show(renderer="notebook")
else:
    print("Cost plot unavailable: No pricing available.")

fig = px.scatter(
    summary, x="P50 ms", y="Macro F1", color="Display",
    labels={"Display": "Run"},
    hover_data=["Provider", "Model", "Accuracy", "Coverage", "P95 ms", "Records"],
    title="Macro F1 versus median request latency",
)
fig.update_traces(marker_size=14)
fig.show(renderer="notebook")
```

languages = pl.DataFrame([

])

## Prediction disagreements

Only records where the runs predict different labels are shown. `unresolved`
means a provider failed to return a label. Agreement can include shared mistakes;
it is not a substitute for comparing against reference labels.

```{python}
if comparison["disagreements"]:
    show_table(pl.DataFrame(comparison["disagreements"]))
else:
    print("No prediction disagreements on these records.")
```

## Usage and provenance

```{python}
show_table(pl.DataFrame([
    {
        "Run": run["label"],
        "Input tokens": run["metrics"]["usage_input_tokens_total"],
        "Output tokens": run["metrics"]["usage_output_tokens_total"],
        "Usage fraction": run["metrics"]["usage_records_fraction"],
        "Known USD": run["metrics"]["cost_usd_known_total"],
    }
    for run in runs
]))
show_table(pl.DataFrame([
    {
        "Run": run["label"], "Source folder": run["path"],
        "Prompt": run["prompt_version"],
        "Simulated": run["simulated"],
        "Historical input verified": run["historical_input_verified"],
    }
    for run in runs
]))
```

Token totals sum known usage; missing usage does not imply a free request. These
results use synthetic financial feedback with template variations. Exact
matching does not establish independence or real-world generalization.
